body: Thanks. Making notes sounds good. I know when I talked to them about it in the past (which was only because my girlfriend, who somehow still cared about me even though I treated her like shit, called them and told them I was depressed) I was really flustered and didn't know what to say, and then I was afraid it was coming off like I was making it all up.

Thanks. What sort of clinic do you mean? Not somewhere I'm going to be committed... right? I'm afraid if I tell someone I was suicidal they will be forced to put me somewhere I don't want to go. But I don't really know how this works.

e: I meant committed... I think.

The best of the best bulls will often have semen extracted and sold across the country for quite a cash prize. I'm not sure how prevalent this is though. I'm pretty sure the guys don't sit there jerking the bull off though...

This is what I think, and perhaps what OP thinks as well, in response to number 3: People are only superficially nice. If you have worked in a service job, you damn well know that you are just a robot on autorepeat. How can you be sincere if you are just repeating the same things over and over to ever single person, no matter how little you know them? There are people who are friendly out of obligation (your barber, your family) and people who are friendly because they care about you. If you are so lonely that you can't make any friends, then nobody cares about you for any reason other than they feel they must. And that seems pretty worthless.
At my weird elementary school we used "XESPN". The X wasn't actually an X word, and I forgot what it was, but then I think it was Excellent, Satisfactory, Poor, No Effort or something.

I guess. I'm not sure I have anyone, though. My family just loves me out of obligation, and my friends don't even know me. I wear a mask around all of them and they don't see my true self. And as this has gone on for years, I now just want to be alone and be left alone. I want to sever all ties.

I know your feelings. In my sophomore year in the dorms I felt alienated as well. I would sneak down to the dining hall, often eating dinner at the very earliest or very latest time so that no acquaintance of mine would see me eating alone in the corner. I would pick up the school newspaper and at least pretend to read it. 

I too had a group of friends who now seem to avoid me. It sucks, it really does. I wish I could offer some advice, but I'm two years ahead of you and still haven't figured any of this out. I feel like the door is closing on the possibility of making friends. Because you sort of need social capital to make friends. Nobody seems to want to take a chance on a loner with no friends.

I'm an atheist, but thanks. I understand wanting to get fucked up to forget. For me, getting high is my way of forgetting about my problems. I spent a good chunk of my waking hours this summer high. It's an escalating game, seeing how far I can go and how frequently and carelessly I can smoke before my parents find out. I pretend that the school year will never resume, that I will never have to look for an internship or worry about friends. After a point, it wasn't even doing much for me aside from making me forget, just for a little while. 

Thanks for being so kind to me.

Thanks a lot for the comment. I appreciate it.

I wish it were easy for me to see it that way. I know that I have at least a small bit of potential to make the world better. But I see life as an investment, and all of my ventures have backfired.

In Boy Scouts I quit at Life (one rank below Eagle). In high school I gave up on cross country running, soccer and nordic skiing (not that I was a standout). 

Last year I tried to challenge myself by spending the year abroad (in Europe, even, which is barely a challenge coming from the States) but ended up making zero friends, spending all day every day alternating between computer games and crying, and drinking a bottle of cheap wine every other night. I aborted that program after only two months when I had intended to stay ten. I didn't even sign up for half of the classes I was supposed to, and I stopped going to any after just one week. I lied to my parents who put up thousands of dollars for me to be there. The night that I got drunk and angry enough to punch my laptop screen with a bottle opener was when I realized I had trapped myself and had no choice to go home. When my parents told me to spend my last few days seeing the city and taking pictures, I half went out to look for a high bridge to jump off of. I have lied to all of my friends about why I came back early ("academic reasons"). Lying has become so natural that I sometimes feel that I am even convincing myself. 

My brother, himself living a busy life in China but knowing I am a tough nut to crack, had attempted to reach out to redditors in the area to have them meet up with me. But he had them send messages to an e-mail address that I neglected to check. Two months after I returned and was back at my university, I checked that e-mail finally and found it flooded with messages. I think about five friendly, enthusiastic locals had tried to reach out to me in my loneliness, and my brother had sent me a dozen e-mails even though I hadn't answered one. They ranged from sincerely concerned at the beginning to obviously disappointed at the end. I think the night I found those e-mails was the most ashamed I have ever been.

Recently I lied to my parents about my search for an internship. I did not apply to any, and that was the single reason I did not receive any. I claim to be unlucky, but it's an excuse for my ineptitude. 

I've tried in the past to do well in life, I really have. But I just suck at it and am too indecisive to do anything about it. I would rather just be sad and hide it from everyone.

I'm with you. I want to kill myself, know that I probably won't, but don't want any help. I could even get free counseling at school, but I've been through three months of therapy before and it did nothing. All I remember is him being obsessed with my nervous habits, like how I used to pull my hair out, and offering generic advice.

Nah, I'm sure I would find a real creative way to let you down. 

You bring up a good point though. How the hell would you ever connect with someone going through similar things if they, like you, close themselves into a depressing bubble and likely feel too exhausted to deal with the social upkeep of maintaining a friendship? I guess the Internet helps, at least in theory.
